facts: Section 2.1 (printed p. 6370) trains the new encoder while retaining already computed old gallery embeddings.
Section 2.2, Eq. (2) evaluates new-model query features against old-model gallery features.
Section 2.4, Eqs. (7)-(8), trains new model parameters with an influence loss using the fixed old classifier; Section 2.5 leaves old model parameters unchanged.

uses.claim: Backward-compatible representation learning trains a new encoder to remain usable with previously computed gallery features.
uses.reason: This is exactly the BCT direction: optimize the new encoder so its query features can be searched against fixed, previously computed old gallery features. Sections 2.1-2.2 and Eq. (2) explicitly establish new-query/old-gallery evaluation; Section 2.4 explains training through the fixed old classifier. The cited sentence neither reverses the direction nor claims post-hoc mapping of old documents to a destination space.
